LESSON: CONTROLLING SOIL EROSION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: CONSERVATION OF RESOURCES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested
Topic 1.1: Controlling Soil Erosion

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Controlling Soil Erosion. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does erosion control conserve the environment?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe types of soil erosion in the environment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONTROLLING SOIL EROSION
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Controlling Soil Erosion helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CONTROLLING SOIL EROSION
Controlling Soil Erosion is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Describe types of soil erosion in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe types of soil erosion in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe types of soil erosion in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Controlling Soil Erosion” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe types of soil erosion in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Controlling Soil Erosion is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Controlling Soil Erosion” around your school. (skill: describe types of soil erosion in the environment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Controlling Soil Erosion to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe types of soil erosion in the environment.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Controlling Soil Erosion from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Controlling Soil Erosion: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Controlling Soil Erosion?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does erosion control conserve the environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Controlling Soil Erosion means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe types of soil erosion in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
